page: Amazon Web Services i8ge.3xlarge is an arm64 storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by AWS Graviton processors with ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture. The instance features 12 dedicated physical cores and 12 vCPUs operating at 2.8 GHz, with 1 thread per core. The processor subsystem includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware acceleration for AES cryptography. The server does not include x86 vector extensions such as AVX or AMX.

Memory capacity is configured at 96.0 GB, providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Benchmarks indicate superior memory subsystem throughput, with PassMark memory performance landing in the top 10 percent and uncached large-block read and write bandwidth reaching 210.54 GB/sec and 109.34 GB/sec, respectively. Dedicated storage comprises 7,500 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, while baseline network throughput is rated at 12 Gbps. The instance does not include discrete GPU accelerators.

Compute benchmarks reflect balanced mid-range performance, scoring 1,889.0 in Geekbench single-core and 12,945.0 in multi-core tests. While bzip3 single-threaded decompression registers in the top 25 percent, encryption tests and LLM inference generation yield lower-tier results due to the lack of specialized matrix extensions. The configuration offers strong resource density for disk- and memory-intensive applications, making it well matched for distributed databases, caching tiers, data ingestion pipelines, and local real-time analytics.
description: Amazon Web Services i8ge.3xlarge is a storage-optimized instance featuring 12 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores at 2.8 GHz, 96.0 GB of system memory, and 7,500 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance delivers an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, 12 Gbps baseline networking, and top-tier memory bandwidth exceeding 210 GB/sec on uncached reads. Synthetic tests demonstrate average overall multi-core compute capability alongside robust memory and decompression throughput, though cryptographic and AI token generation workloads demonstrate weaker results due to the absence of dedicated matrix instructions. Lacking discrete GPUs, the system delivers dense local storage and substantial RAM, making it tailored for high-throughput databases, search clusters, distributed caching, and heavy I/O operations.
